Absent that, this is a deleveraging that pays the preferred and the lenders while the common funds the manager's next acquisition. Not a macro bet; the flaw is structural, not directional. Downside is severe and asymmetric: 7.0x on the low guide ($620m) leaves $0.94bn equity = $6.05/sh, and 6.0x leaves ~$2/sh, because at 5.9x leverage small EV moves annihilate the stub - Q2-2026 already printed a $187m GAAP net loss, revenue -17%, and a 23% cut to FY26 adj EBITDA. One unresolved gap I could not close within the lookup budget (web-search quota was exhausted): the 30.1m new shares are ~24% of the 125.2m pre-deal count, above the NYSE 312.03(c) 20% threshold that normally compels a shareholder vote, yet the release discloses no special meeting - either the structure avoids it or a vote is an undisclosed gate; verify against the 8-K/investment agreement before sizing. This is genuine balance-sheet repair with a named strategic anchor, and it deserves a WATCH seat, but it is not takeout arb and the honest event capture is ~5%, not 27%.
